## What it does
SlopSieve adds a small verdict badge next to posts in your feed, labelling the ones that look like bot-generated, AI-generated, or low-quality content. Click any badge to see the breakdown — which signals fired, the account's score, the text's score, and the combined meta-verdict.
The goal is a quieter feed. Pick one of three modes from the toolbar popup: **Off** just shows the badges, **Dim** fades flagged posts so you can hover to read them, and **Hide** collapses them to a small click-to-show stub.
## Why it's different
* **On-device scoring**The ML model runs inside your browser. Your feed is not sent to a server for scoring.
* **Multi-platform**One extension covers X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Reddit (new + old), and Hacker News. Same verdict model, consistent badges.
* **No telemetry**No analytics, no heartbeats, no third-party SDKs. Scoring makes zero background requests.

Redd-Eye (Reddit AI & Bot Detection) – Get this Extension for 🦊 Firefox (en-US)

Redd Eye: AI and Bot DetectionRedd Eye is an open source extension created to flag suspected bot accounts and AI generated content on Reddit in real time. Whether you use the modern layout or old reddit, it integrates right into your feed to help you spot inauthentic activity at a glance.Key Features

- Real Time Detection: Scan and flag AI text and bot like behavior as you scroll through threads and comments.
- Visual Indicators: It uses color coded outlines and quick popups so you can instantly spot suspicious activity right on the page.
- Customizable Thresholds: You have full control. You can fine tune the sensitivity of both the AI and Bot detection algorithms to match your preferences using the built in sliders.
- Adjustable UI: Move the settings widget to any corner of your screen so it never blocks your browsing.
- Seamless Compatibility: It works across both the standard reddit interface and old reddit.

Privacy FirstYour data belongs to you. Redd Eye operates entirely locally on your machine. There is absolutely zero data collection, zero telemetry, and no hidden subscriptions. # How to Detect AI on Reddit - Fighting the Bots

How moderators and readers can detect AI-generated posts and comments on Reddit, and why subreddits like r/writing ban AI slop outright.

Alex Roitman

▪ Feb 6, 2026

Reddit has become a primary search destination because users want helpful information from real people, rather than generic information.

For now, Google’s core updates favor Reddit. There is one problem with this, though: LLMs are increasingly being used to flood subreddits with “mention activity” and citations. Both of these things are designed to boost the search visibility of a particular brand, individual, or entity.

If you’re trying to detect AI on Reddit, you don’t have to rely on a gut feeling. We will cover manual linguistic tells for AI detection on Reddit and go over how the Pangram Chrome Extension provides an instant verification layer for any post.

Why is AI Content Spiking on Reddit?

Reddit is a high-authority platform for “mention activity” - users mentioning a specific brand, individual, or entity. AI content is spiking on Reddit because brands and spammers use LLMs to create artificial social proof and cite specific products to influence search rankings. Doing so is meant to bring more people to their products

# Reddit LLM Comment Detector

A browser extension that uses machine learning to detect AI-generated comments on Reddit. Built with 🤗 Transformers.js for client-side inference.

## 🎯 What It Does

This extension analyzes Reddit comments in real-time to identify content that may have been generated by Large Language Models (AI). It provides:

- **🚨 Visual highlighting** of potentially AI-generated comments
- **📊 User scoring system** that tracks AI detection percentages for individual users 
- **🎨 Color-coded risk levels** (green/orange/red based on AI percentage)
- **💾 Persistent tracking** across browsing sessions
- **⚡ Real-time analysis** as you browse Reddit
- **🎛️ Customizable aggression levels** from passive highlighting to auto-minimizing AI comments
